title: Frozen persistence gate improves sampled downside score under both latency conditions
research_question: Does a fixed minimum predicted quote persistence of 0.90 improve the downside objective against deterministic and no-trade controls on unused source groups?
hypothesis: Quote-persistence filtering reduces execution-risk tail losses despite missing some profitable opportunities.
interpretation: The frozen logistic persistence gate scores 0.904 at baseline versus arbitrage 0.281 and no-trade zero. Added 200ms delay lowers its score to 0.765, still above the sampled controls. Mean P&L is lower than arbitrage at baseline (paired difference -0.578, grouped 95% interval [-0.845, -0.319]); the higher downside score reflects smaller observed tail loss, not higher mean return. Paired mean versus no-trade remains positive under delay (0.925, interval [0.502, 1.407]). Delay reduces gate mean by 0.139, interval [-0.255, -0.046]. Worst gate loss is -2.4 in both conditions. This supports a bounded synthetic decision-policy benefit, not real profitability or broad robustness.
caveats: Quote persistence cannot establish two-leg completion
Both conditions share 100 source groups, not 3000 independent samples
Input-support ranges do not establish joint calibration
Hypothetical synthetic economics and action-dependent execution noise
Directed research evaluation; champion promotion withheld
Both conditions share the same 100 independent source groups.
Input support abstention increased under delay; this is not evidence of calibrated fill probability.
Champion promotion was withheld by preregistration; challenge outcomes changed no weights or thresholds.
These two conditions do not establish fee, financing, distribution-shift or recovery robustness.
next_experiment: Preserve this frozen policy evidence, then examine risk/cost labels and recovery semantics on separately preregistered scenarios. Do not retune this gate on the opened challenge.
